items.item: The model sheets, boards, finished scenes and colour script implement the specification's chosen visual approach, allowing the expected differences between planning drawings and finished rendering.
Colour and lighting support the supplied blue-green underwater light, suspended particles and depth atmosphere while preserving recognizable character and envelope features.
Locations, subject positions, travel direction and camera staging remain compatible with the route map and the shot table across all depictions.
The S03/S04, S05/S06 and S07/S08 transition pairs preserve both moving subjects and make arch separation, rising pursuit and the change from bubble grip to hand possession understandable.
Storyboard shots, colour panels and the two finished keyframes depict compatible moments of the same nine-shot action sequence.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The specification occupies one page and states a coherent visual approach, the Loss/Pursuit/Delivery act structure, nine individually timed shots, both tether activations, all three permanent character features and both envelope lines. It states a maximum activation distance of 300 mm from the releasing hand to the letter, a two-second grip and four seconds of recovery after each release. Anatomy and architectural styling may be chosen freely. Missing required information or altered world rules fails.

Both written records enumerate S01 through S09 once, in order, with durations 2/2/2/2/2/1/1/1/2 seconds and a total of 15 seconds. The specification gives respective start–end intervals 0–2, 2–4, 4–6, 6–8, 8–10, 10–11, 11–12, 12–13 and 13–15 seconds. Act 1 contains S01, Act 2 S02–S05 and Act 3 S06–S09. A changed duration, missing shot, overlapping beat or incorrect total fails.

The sheets contain exactly three shot panels each: S01–S03, S04–S06 and S07–S09 respectively, with an unambiguous reading order across sheets. Every panel internally prints its own shot ID, a WS/MS/CU designation, duration in seconds and the character name Pip. Durations follow 2/2/2/2/2/1/1/1/2 seconds. Framing choices are open within the permitted vocabulary; omitted, displaced or conflicting panel metadata fails.

There are nine shot records, each with an ID, WS/MS/CU size, duration, Pip as character, action, sound, camera movement and separate entry and exit positions for Pip and the envelope. A stationary camera may be explicitly recorded. Actions preserve loss in S01, kelp extraction in S02, expiry and separated arch routes in S03–S04, rising pursuit in S05, second activation in S06, drawing the letter close in S07, hand capture in S08 and full slot insertion in S09. Sound follows the supplied water, fin-stroke, kelp-brushing, tether-tension and bubble-pop palette where applicable. Missing fields, conflated subjects or reassigned story events fails.

Each document explicitly states nine shots, a 15-second runtime, Mara Vale and 7 Lantern Reef. The presentation cover displays BRINE EXPRESS, and its story page reproduces the complete Synopsis paragraph from 03-story-records.en.md. Typographic wrapping may vary; paraphrasing, truncation, changed wording, incorrect facts or placing the title only on an interior page fails.

The sheet clearly supplies front, side and back views of one character and three distinguishable expressions. The design establishes a mustard shoulder satchel, a white patch on Pip's anatomical left elbow and exactly three coral-red head fins. Hidden features need not be visible through the body. Anatomy, proportions, facial structure and swimming style are open; missing views, insufficient expressions or inconsistent permanent features fails.

Front, back and edge views describe one envelope with dimensions explicitly recorded as 160 mm wide and 100 mm high and a corresponding 8:5 face proportion. It reads as warm ivory waterproof paper. The front legibly carries Mara Vale and 7 Lantern Reef; the back closure has a teal wax seal with a raised spiral. Water damage occupies the lower-right corner from the front and the corresponding lower-left corner from the back. Perspective is allowed; missing construction views, reversed damage, incorrect dimensions or relocated lettering or closure fails.

The map labels all five stations, separate Pip and letter paths, camera positions and the eastbound Y=0 action axis. Station X coordinates are 0, 2000, 4000, 6000 and 8000 mm respectively, all at Y=0. Both subjects begin at depth 3000 mm; at Shell Arch the letter remains at 3000 mm while Pip uses the 4000 mm lower passage; Bubble Chimney raises both from 3000 to 2000 mm; Lantern House and its 200-by-30-mm mail slot are at 2000 mm. Cameras lie within X=-1000 to 9000 mm, Y=-4000 to -1000 mm and depth 1000 to 5000 mm. Across the boards, eastward travel reads left to right, the letter leads before S07, and upper/lower passages and upward current agree with the map. Schematic drawing and perspective are allowed; reversed geography, missing depth information, crossed camera territory or incompatible paths fails.

The visual sequence agrees with the specification: kelp catches the envelope corner and motivates the S02 grip at 2–4 seconds; that grip expires at 4 seconds, followed by recovery through S03–S04 at 4–8 seconds. Pip follows the arch's lower route while the envelope passes through the upper opening, and the chimney current raises both. S05 closes the gap; a second grip starts in S06 at 10 seconds and continues through S07 until 12 seconds. Both activations occur within 300 mm of Pip's releasing hand. S08 visibly transfers possession to the hand and turns the addressed face toward the viewer; S09 makes that face readable before ending with no envelope protruding from the slot. Sequential poses or clear motion annotations may convey action on static sheets; unexplained rescue, premature reactivation, teleportation or partial final insertion fails.

Across all depicted views, visible character features retain the mustard shoulder satchel, white patch on the anatomical left elbow and three coral-red head fins. Lighting, expression, pose and perspective may vary, and occluded features are exempt. Moving the patch to the right elbow, changing the fin count or losing or recolouring a visible permanent feature fails.

Recognizable envelope depictions preserve the model's 8:5 face proportions, teal spiral back seal and water-darkened front lower-right corner, corresponding to the lower-left corner when seen from behind. Visible front text uses Mara Vale and 7 Lantern Reef, and both lines are fully readable in the delivery keyframe. Perspective, underwater lighting, occlusion and reduced detail at small scale are allowed; mirrored damage, changed identifying marks, conflicting readable text or an illegible delivery-keyframe address fails.

Read the table alongside the images: every board panel matches its row's ID, shot-size designation, duration and Pip character entry. The colour script covers S01–S09 exactly once. The chimney keyframe depicts S06 and the delivery keyframe depicts S09. The continuity sheet identifies S03/S04, S05/S06 and S07/S08 and tracks both Pip and the envelope on both sides of each cut, including position, direction and possession where relevant. Missing subjects, mismatched metadata, wrong shot assignments or discontinuous transfers fails.

Each storyboard shot frame and each keyframe uses a 16:9 composition. Essential action remains within the inset 3.5% action boundary on all four edges, and printed graphics remain within the inset 5% graphic boundary. Judge individual shot frames rather than the outer storyboard-sheet proportions. Background scenery may extend to the frame edge; cropped action or graphics intruding into the protected margins fails.

The document identifies 16:9 as the main composition and 9:16 as a future adaptation, with action insets of 3.5% and graphic insets of 5% on every edge of each. It reserves 8–10 seconds for optional descriptive narration and preserves the silent physical performance premise. No completed portrait adaptation or recorded narration is required. Missing a composition, swapping margin values or reserving a different interval fails.

Both images are resolved colour-and-light scenes following the stated visual approach and model designs. The chimney image stages S06's second tether activation at the upper exit; the delivery image stages S09 at Lantern House's slot with the addressed face legible before insertion. Blue-green underwater illumination, suspended particles and depth atmosphere reflect the supplied lighting direction. Composition and architectural styling are open; rough unresolved staging, a wrong location or beat, or incompatible character or envelope design fails.

Nine ordered colour panels are individually labelled S01–S09 and correspond to each board shot's location, principal action and subject relationship. Colour and lighting develop a coherent underwater sequence while retaining the established character and envelope identifiers. Simplified rendering and colour exploration are allowed; missing or repeated shots, a location swap or an action incompatible with the corresponding board fails.

Review the complete video and audio against the written and visual sources. It runs 15 seconds with nine ordered shots lasting 2/2/2/2/2/1/1/1/2 seconds at boundaries 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 15. Verify the five-station route and attached depths, south-side camera territory, left-to-right travel, envelope lead before S07, separate arch passages and chimney ascent. Verify kelp-motivated grip at 2–4 seconds, four-dot recovery at 4–8 seconds, second grip at 10–12 seconds, activation within 300 mm, transparent gripping bubble and luminous hand tether, S08 hand capture, readable addressed front before S09 insertion and an entirely inserted final envelope. Recovery follows each release, with no requirement to extend the film beyond 15 seconds. Visible Pip and envelope identifiers must match their models. Shot compositions are 16:9 with 3.5% action and 5% graphic insets. Water movement, swimming/fin strokes and bubble sounds are audible, with kelp brushing and tether tension supporting their events; physical performance is silent and 8–10 seconds contains no speech. Any contradictory timing, geography, mechanism, ending, identity, safe-area treatment or required sound omission fails.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation visibly incorporates recognizable material from every listed source, including each storyboard sheet, both keyframes and still frames from the delivered animatic. Scaling, readable excerpts, cropping and page-layout changes are allowed when the original work remains identifiable. Merely naming a deliverable, substituting unrelated artwork or omitting any source fails.

The presentation has at least eight pages and individually accounts for all nine shots. Its account assigns the escape to S01, kelp extraction to S02, grip expiry and upper/lower arch separation to S03, lower passage and letter entry into the rising current to S04, Pip's rising pursuit and approach within range to S05, second activation to S06, drawing the gripped letter close to S07, release into the hand and addressed-front turn to S08, and readable-front presentation followed by complete insertion to S09. Page design and grouping are open; an undersized presentation, omitted shot or altered event assignment fails.

Whenever an active grip is depicted, one transparent bubble encloses the envelope and a luminous tether visibly connects it to Pip's hand. Linework or annotations may communicate transparency and luminosity in planning sheets; finished imagery resolves them visually. Images without an active-grip beat are exempt. Multiple gripping bubbles, an unattached tether or a grip that hides the envelope's identity fails.

The recovery sequence establishes four wrist dots at release and communicates one dot fading per elapsed second. During the first recovery, S03 progresses from four to two dots and S04 removes the final two. Static poses, successive panels or explicit timing annotations may establish the progression; wrist occlusion is allowed. Later visible recovery states must remain compatible with the same rule. A missing recovery cue throughout the relevant sequence, reversed progression or readiness before four seconds fails.

The model sheets, boards, finished scenes and colour script implement the specification's chosen visual approach, allowing the expected differences between planning drawings and finished rendering. Colour and lighting support the supplied blue-green underwater light, suspended particles and depth atmosphere while preserving recognizable character and envelope features.

Locations, subject positions, travel direction and camera staging remain compatible with the route map and the shot table across all depictions. The S03/S04, S05/S06 and S07/S08 transition pairs preserve both moving subjects and make arch separation, rising pursuit and the change from bubble grip to hand possession understandable. Storyboard shots, colour panels and the two finished keyframes depict compatible moments of the same nine-shot action sequence.
